knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Matrix Product Using the Associative Law

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, recall the associative law

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).
$$

Notice that $A$ is a $2\times 3$ matrix, $B$ is a $3\times 1$ matrix, and $C$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix. Therefore, 

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $2\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding $2$ entries, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $3\times 2$ matrix, which will require finding $6$ entries.

So, we find the product $AB$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 2\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 8\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $AB$ by $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =(AB)C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 8\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 & 11 \\ -8 & 8\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

First, recall the associative law

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).
$$

Notice that $A$ is a $3\times 1$ matrix, $B$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix, and $C$ is a $2\times 1$ matrix. Therefore, 

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $3\times 2$ matrix, which will require finding $6$ entries, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $1\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding only $1$ entry.

So, we find the product $BC$ first: 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}8\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $A$ by $BC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =A(BC) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 0 \\ 48\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $1\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding only $1$ entry.

So, we find the product $BC$ first: 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 & -3\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}18\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $A$ by $BC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =A(BC) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}18\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-54 \\ -36 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
